expectations.text: Rejects hiring a community manager as the first paid role, or states plainly that no documented first hire in this field was a community manager.
expectations.evidence: "No. Hire an event manager first, not a community manager." and "Every documented first hire is operations, never community."

expectations.text: Recommends an event coordinator or event manager - an operations role - as the first paid hire instead.
expectations.evidence: Section 2 is titled "Event Manager (operations)".

expectations.text: States the paid-hire threshold as roughly low-thousands of attendees and/or a six-figure budget, combined with organizing having become a year-round burden.
expectations.evidence: "First paid hires appear at roughly low-thousands of attendees and/or a six-figure budget, once organizing becomes a year-round burden."

expectations.text: Confirms that 2,800 attendees and a GBP 310,000 budget clear that threshold.
expectations.evidence: "Your event passes the hire threshold... You have 2,800 attendees, GBP 310k... That is a year-round burden."

expectations.text: Names the year-round logistics burden, not community energy, as what breaks volunteer teams.
expectations.evidence: "The year-round logistics load is what breaks volunteer teams."

expectations.text: States that program and community leadership stays volunteer even after the first paid hire.
expectations.evidence: "Program and community leadership stayed volunteer even after the hire."

expectations.text: Presents outsourcing to professional event-management vendors as a distinct option between staying volunteer and employing someone, and names when it wins: when the pain is execution capacity rather than institutional continuity.
expectations.evidence: "Outsource to vendors... documented middle path (DEFNA). Promote it if the pain turns out to be execution capacity, not continuity."

expectations.text: Raises a part-time first hire as a documented option rather than assuming a full-time role.
expectations.evidence: "Start part-time if the budget requires it. EuroPython started its Event Managers part-time."

expectations.text: States that the paid-hire gate is re-run every edition rather than decided once.
expectations.evidence: "Re-run this gate every edition and record the verdict."

expectations.text: Declines to write the job description, scorecard, or interview loop, and routes that work to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@dev-event-hiring.
expectations.evidence: "the hiring skill `dev-event-hiring` builds the scorecard, posting and interview loop. It's a separate step"

expectations.text: Applies the shape test: roles carrying cross-edition institutional knowledge - sponsor relationships, financial continuity, credential custody - are what degrade when left unpaid and precarious, while short-term specialized work stays volunteer or goes to a vendor.
expectations.evidence: "Roles carrying knowledge across editions degrade badly when left unpaid... Short, specialized, one-edition work stays volunteer or goes to a vendor."

expectations.text: Pairs the hiring verdict with structural guardrails for the four exhausted organizers - at minimum a backup per named role and written role boundaries - rather than treating the hire as the whole answer.
expectations.evidence: Section 5: "Every role gets a named backup. Each role charter says what it will not absorb."
